prompt: We're building an order-processing pipeline and need to pick a message queue. It's between AWS SQS (managed, dead simple) and self-hosting RabbitMQ on our existing cluster (more control, supports complex routing we might need later). Orders are business-critical and we can't lose messages. Write up an RFC so the team can decide.
assertions: Has a contextualization section describing the current state, written for a newcomer (no prior knowledge assumed)
Requirements are present and explicitly split into functional and non-functional
Every requirement states the goal or rationale it serves, not just the requirement text
Every non-functional requirement carries a quantified metric and target (a number with a unit), not an adjective
Every requirement names how its fulfilment will be proven or verified at the end
The no-message-loss requirement is expressed measurably (a durability target, an acceptable loss rate, or a verification method) rather than as a slogan
Design section names the components and includes or precisely describes at least one static diagram AND at least one dynamic (flow/sequence) diagram
Tradeoff analysis compares both named alternatives (AWS SQS vs self-hosted RabbitMQ) with pros and cons
Tradeoff analysis includes at least one credible alternative the user did not propose
Every risk in the tradeoff analysis carries all four attributes (impact, probability, mitigation, contingency), each with a reason or fact behind it; a bare 'unknown', 'TBD' or 'N/A' does not count
States an explicit decision (which alternative was chosen) rather than leaving it open
Records the consequences of the decision and how it will be confirmed later (a metric, check, or review)
Includes a conclusion with a rollout/launch strategy or a task roadmap
Written entirely in English (matching the request language)
